chapter_name: Short Writing Skills: Notices, Messages, and Dialogue
learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of writing quick, clear, and catchy messages and notices that give all the facts without wasting any words!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A Notice is a formal announcement written to inform a group of people about an event, competition, or lost item. Rule #1: It MUST be put inside a BOX! Rule #2: Keep it under 50 words. No long stories, just facts!

main_concepts.concept_title: 📐 The 5 W's of a Perfect Notice
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every good notice must answer 5 W's: WHAT is the event? WHEN is it happening (date and time)? WHERE is it happening (venue)? WHO can participate? and WHOM to contact for details? If you have these 5, you get full marks!

A message is a short piece of information you write for someone when you cannot speak to them directly (like a sticky note on the fridge). It also goes in a BOX! Write the Date, Time, Name of receiver, the short message, and your Name at the end. Cut the greetings, get straight to the point!

Dialogue is a written conversation between two or more people. It needs to sound natural, like real people talking! Use contractions (can't, don't) and exclamation marks for emotion. Make sure each person takes turns speaking logically.

main_concepts.concept_title: ✂️ The Golden Rule of Short Writing
main_concepts.simple_explanation: KISS: Keep It Short and Simple! Do not use heavy vocabulary or extra sentences in notices and messages. The goal is to deliver information fast. If you go over the word limit, you lose marks!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Lost Pet Notice
fun_activity.instructions: Pretend you lost your pet dinosaur! Write a quick 40-word Notice. Put it in a box. Mention the colour, size, where you lost it, and what the reward is for finding it!

quick_recap: ⭐ Notices and Messages MUST always be drawn inside a box.
⭐ A Notice is formal and answers the 5 Ws: What, When, Where, Who, and Whom.
⭐ A Message is informal and brief (e.g., taking a phone message for your mom).
⭐ Dialogue writing should sound like a natural, flowing conversation.
⭐ Stick strictly to the 50-word limit for both Notices and Messages!
